Research Profile

My research focuses on the design of mechanisms and robotic systems that optimise mechanical energy interactions — including those stored in springs, weights, and magnets — to enable next-generation technologies. I am globally recognised for my impact in static balancing and gravity compensation of mechanisms and robots. My research programme spans mechanism and machine design broadly, encompassing linkage synthesis, parallel manipulators, reconfigurable mechanisms, robotic actuators, rehabilitation devices, and surgical robotics. I have authored more than 100 peer-reviewed publications and hold 4 granted US patents, two of which have been transferred to industry.

Editorship

I have held editorial leadership positions in several of the world's most respected journals in mechanical design, mechanisms, and robotics. Serving as Associate Editor for ASME Journal of Mechanical Design, ASME Journal of Mechanisms and Robotics, and Mechanism and Machine Theory — widely regarded as the leading journals in mechanisms and machine science — represents a rare distinction that reflects international recognition of my scholarly standing and leadership in advancing the discipline.

Teaching & Academic Activities

Courses Taught

I regularly teach core subjects in mechanical and mechatronic engineering, including Mechanical Design and Dynamics of Mechanisms. At UOW, I regularly teach Mechanical Design 1 & 2 (MMMB215 & MECH311) and Dynamics of Mechanisms (MECH326). I also consistently support the Fly-in-Fly-Out teaching of UOW's twinning programs offered at Beijing Jiaotong University and Taiyuan University of Technology in China. In addition, I have taught a wide range of subjects at undergraduate and postgraduate levels, including:
